pushSpellings.refused: ennyn: this reaches a push outside the shape Claude Code's ask rule reads for certain: {command}. Write the push in a call of its own, `git push <remote> <branch>`, or `cd <folder> && git push <remote> <branch>` from another folder, with the commit in the call before. A call that pushes holds plain words joined by `&&`, `;`, `|`, `>` or a newline, and nothing else: one quote, `$`, comment, parenthesis, brace, backtick, backslash, `<` or lone `&` anywhere in it refuses it. Unless push.mode is after-closing, this hook then asks the user; else ask first if nobody has approved this push. If this is no push, tell the user the hook misread it.

pushSpellings.subagent: ennyn: a subagent does not push: this push is refused, never asked, since an ask made in a subagent can wait with nobody there to answer. Leave the push to the main thread, where the cycle's closing asks the user. A lab's upstream is set with fetch, never with a push: `git init -q --bare -b main up.git && git -C up.git fetch -q ../repo main:main && cd repo && git remote add origin ../up.git && git fetch -q origin && git branch -q -u origin/main`.
pushSpellings.unread: ennyn: the push hook could not read this shell command, so a push spelled another way is not refused here; the project's ask rule, if it has one, still stands. A Claude Code update may have changed what hooks are given: update the plugin.
killTargets.refused: ennyn: this stops a process chosen by a filter, a name, a window title, a port or a PID looked up at run time, which can reach the user's own programs: {command}. Stop only a process you started, by its PID or process group, written as a number: `kill <pid>`, `kill -- -<pgid>`, `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`, `Stop-Process -Id <pid>`; in one call, `kill $pid` after `pid=$!`, `kill $(cat <pid file you wrote>)` and `Stop-Process -Id $p.Id` after `$p = Start-Process …` pass. If you do not know which PID you started, ask the user; do not look one up by name or port. If this is no such kill, tell the user the hook misread it.
killTargets.beside: ennyn: the kill word `{word}` stands in a command that also holds `{beside}`, which can make a word into a program when the command runs, so the hook cannot tell what it stops: {command}. Split it: run the part that names `{word}` (the kill, or a grep pattern or message that only mentions it) as a call of its own, with no function definition, `eval`, `source` or `.`, `set`, `xargs` or `$variable` in a program's place beside it. To stop a process you started, write its PID as a number: `kill <pid>`, or `kill $pid` after `pid=$!` in the same call.

In a plugin session a hook refuses every push but a plain git push with literal words at the head of a top-level command, in a text under 9,000 characters of plain words and list separators: the spellings on the ask rules' line and an alias set in the command or the session's environment among them; left are an alias in a config file, a script that pushes, an interpreter, gh api and an MCP tool, and it is no boundary: a program set on pushing gets through, and a hook that crashes or times out lets the call run

lock.roomCeiling: lock: still short of room after {minutes} minutes ({short}); starting anyway
lock.roomUnmeasured: lock: unmeasured, so not waited for: {what}
lock.roomSet: lock: room thresholds set away from the defaults: {set}
lock.ticketGone: lock: this waiter's ticket in {dir} was removed by another waiter; no turn can come to it, so the wait ends
lock.queueLink: lock: the queue {queue} is a symbolic link, refused: no ticket was written, nothing in it removed, and the command did not run. Make it a plain folder
worktrees.none: No worktree carries Ennyn's mark (a lock whose reason is ennyn:<cycle>).
worktrees.others: {n} other linked worktrees carry no mark: left alone.
worktrees.incomplete: {n} could not be checked or removed, or carry no mark: each line above says what is true of it.
worktrees.why.gone: its folder is gone, or its .git file does not point back to this repository
worktrees.why.state: git keeps state of its own for it ({names}): an operation in progress, a config or submodules
worktrees.why.flagged: {n} files are marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree, which git status does not look at, {first} first
worktrees.why.notMerged: branch {branch} is not merged: no other branch, tag or remote branch holds its commit
worktrees.why.detached: no branch, tag or other shared ref holds its commit (a detached HEAD): a reflog does not, it goes with its ref
worktrees.why.leftBehind: {n} commits only it holds: its HEAD reflog, ORIG_HEAD, REBASE_HEAD, FETCH_HEAD or its own refs and their reflogs name them, and no shared ref or reflog holds them
worktrees.entry.relocked: git still lists it, locked with its mark again
worktrees.entry.notRelocked: git still lists it, but its mark could not be put back, so git no longer keeps it from pruning
worktrees.entry.dropped: git no longer lists it, and its mark went with that entry
worktrees.folder.left: its folder is back in place, whole
worktrees.why.dup: another of git's worktree entries names the same folder, and git may act on that one
worktrees.why.staged: its index differs from HEAD: a change is staged, or a conflict is unresolved
worktrees.why.gitEntry: {path} is a .git entry: another repository or worktree inside it, which git status does not list
worktrees.why.notInHead: {path} is not in HEAD (untracked or ignored)
worktrees.why.missing: {path}, which HEAD holds, is not on disk as HEAD has it
worktrees.why.link: {path} is a link whose target differs from HEAD's
worktrees.why.mode: {path} has another mode on disk than in HEAD
worktrees.why.special: {path} is a pipe, a socket or a device
worktrees.why.differs: {path} differs from what a checkout of HEAD writes
worktrees.why.changed: {path} changed after it was checked, so what it holds now was not checked
worktrees.folder.changed: its folder, holding a change made after the check, is at {aside}: look at it before you delete it
worktrees.why.movedAside: its folder was moved aside for removal and is at {path}: look, then delete it or move it back
worktrees.why.notMoved: it could not be moved aside for its removal ({error}); nothing was removed
worktrees.why.busy: it could not be moved aside for its removal ({error}): a process may hold a file or its working directory in it; nothing was removed
worktrees.folder.aside: its folder, whole or what a failed delete left of it (which matched HEAD when checked), is at {aside}
agents.noFolder: No Claude Code session transcript for this repository: no session has run at its top, or Claude Code keeps its config elsewhere (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). Give --session <path>.
agents.noSession: No session transcript {session} in this repository's Claude Code folder.
agents.noPath: No session transcript {session} at the path given.
agents.chosenRunning: Read: the session that runs this command (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID).
agents.chosenNewest: Read: the newest transcript in this repository's folder; CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID {why}.
agents.noRunning: The session that runs this command (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) has no transcript in this repository's Claude Code folder. Give --session <id or path>.
agents.mismatch: Mismatch: {n} of the {of} agents that asked for a model ran another: {list}.
agents.match: No mismatch: each of the {n} agents that asked for a model ran it.
agents.notCompared: Not compared: {n} agents, whose ask is default, unknown or no model name, or that made no call.
agents.legend: asked: the Agent call's model, else the agent's record, else its agent file as it is now; default: nothing asked, so the agent's definition or the session's settings decide; unknown: could not be read.
agents.skipped: {n} transcript lines skipped: not JSON, or longer than {max} MB.
agents.unreadRecords: {n} subagent records could not be read as JSON: what those agents asked for is unmeasured.
agents.lastContextUnmeasured: context at the last call unmeasured
agents.aliasRemap: An alias asked for can be mapped to another model by ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL, _OPUS_, _HAIKU_ or _FABLE_MODEL, which the transcript does not record: such a setting is one possible cause.
commits.author: author {address} is not in commits.addresses
commits.otherSigner: signed by a key the allowed-signers file lists for {signer}, not for its committer {address}
commits.unchecked: signed, but git verified no signature here (gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile is not set, or the signature is of another gpg.format)
commits.notGood: git verifies no good signature by a listed key: %G? is {code}, {what}
commits.notSsh: signed with {format}, which commits.signed does not take: git calls such a signature good for any key the local keyring trusts, whatever the allowed-signers file lists
doctor.cloneGaps: commits.*: this clone's git settings would make commits push-check refuses: {settings}; ennyn clone-setup prints what to set
doctor.cloneOk: commits.*: this clone signs and writes its commits as the rule asks (commit and tag signing, an SSH key, an allowed-signers file that lists the signing key for user.email, an address the list holds)
doctor.cloneUnmeasured: commits.*: this clone's git settings are unmeasured: {error}
doctor.cloneKeyUnlisted: commits.*: the allowed-signers file does not list user.signingkey for user.email, so push-check refuses every commit this clone signs; ennyn clone-setup builds the file
doctor.cloneKeyUnmeasured: commits.*: whether the allowed-signers file lists user.signingkey for user.email is unmeasured ({why})
cloneSetup.unset: commits.addresses is empty and commits.signed is false: this clone needs no settings for them.
cloneSetup.commands: commits.addresses: {addresses}; commits.signed: {signed}. Run these in this clone (git config with no --global writes this clone alone):
cloneSetup.noAddress: No address chosen for user.email and the allowed-signers file: name it with --address.
cloneSetup.noLogin: No GitHub login: give --login <login> to build the allowed-signers file from the keys GitHub lists for it.
cloneSetup.baseRefused: ENNYN_GITHUB_API is {base}: only a loopback origin (http://127.0.0.1:<port>) is taken there, so no file was built.
cloneSetup.base: The keys are read from {base} (ENNYN_GITHUB_API), not from GitHub.
cloneSetup.timeout: The SSH signing keys of {login} were not read: no answer in {s} s.
cloneSetup.network: The SSH signing keys of {login} were not read: {error}.
cloneSetup.status: The SSH signing keys of {login} were not read: the answer was HTTP {status}, not 200 (404: no such login).
cloneSetup.tooMany: The SSH signing keys of {login} were not read: they fill more than one page of 100.
cloneSetup.shape: The SSH signing keys of {login} were not read: the answer is not the list the API documents ({why}).
cloneSetup.none: GitHub lists no SSH signing key for {login}: add one (Settings, SSH and GPG keys, key type Signing Key), then run this again.
cloneSetup.written: Wrote {n} SSH signing keys GitHub lists for {login} to {path}, each for {address}.
shape.privateRemedy: Take the private text out or reword it: a tracked file and a commit message reach everyone the repository does. Turning a rule of security.privateText off for this project is a change the loosening check asks the user to approve.
shape.privateRule.literal: a word of this clone's private list, {n} characters
shape.privateRule.address: an address commits.addresses does not hold, {n} characters
shape.privateRule.conversation.dated: the user and a date outside `the user, <YYYY-MM-DD>: a request`, {n} characters
shape.privateRule.conversation.act: an act of the user retold, {n} characters
shape.privateRule.conversation.word: a step put down to the user's word, {n} characters
shape.privateRule.conversation.messages: the user's messages counted or quoted, {n} characters
shape.privateRule.conversation.speaker: a line opened by a speaker's label, {n} characters
shape.privateRule.provenance: a graph source that names the user outside `the user, <YYYY-MM-DD>: a request | approved | left to the session`, {n} characters
cli.privateListUnread: security.privateText's list of private words was not checked: it could not be read ({error}). Fix or remove the file; the other rules ran.
cli.privateListMissing: security.privateText: no word of a private list was checked: security.privateText.listExpected says this project keeps one, and this clone has none at {path} (it lives in the state dir, never in a tracked file). To get one, copy the file from another clone's state dir over a private channel, or run ennyn private-text add (words on stdin, one a line). This commit goes on.
doctor.privateListMissing: security.privateText: the clone {clone} has no list of private words at {path}, and security.privateText.listExpected says the project keeps one, so commit-check checks no listed word here; copy the file from another clone's state dir over a private channel, or run ennyn private-text add
doctor.privateListOk: security.privateText: this clone holds a list of private words, as security.privateText.listExpected asks
doctor.privateListUnread: security.privateText: the list of private words could not be read ({error}), so commit-check checks no listed word; fix or remove the file
cli.privateNamesUnread: security.privateText was not checked in {n} staged path(s) whose names are not UTF-8 ({paths}): git cannot be asked for them by name, so this commit is refused. Give them UTF-8 names, or leave them out of this commit.
cli.privateUnmeasured: security.privateText was not checked: the staged lines could not be read ({error}).
cli.privateReadFailed: security.privateText was not checked in {n} staged path(s) ({paths}): {error}; the other staged files were.
cli.privateHeadUnread: security.privateText: HEAD's version of {n} staged path(s) could not be read ({paths}): {error}; a line there that a move would explain still counts.
cli.privateGraphUnread: security.privateText was not checked for the graph's sources: {paths} could not be read ({error}).
cli.privateGraphNotRead: security.privateText was not checked for the graph's sources: {path} is staged as a {why}, which is no file to read, so this commit is refused.
cli.privateGraphNotJson: security.privateText was not checked for the graph's sources: the staged {path} is no JSON ({error}), so this commit is refused.
privateText.notWord: Nothing was added: line(s) {lines} of the input are no single word (letters and digits, joined by . _ or -).
privateText.none: Nothing was added: no word on stdin (one a line).
privateText.added: Added {n} word(s) to {path}, hashed; {known} already there. commit-check refuses them from now on, in this clone and its worktrees.
